comment: Conformance cases for policy.json (specs/DREAMFERENCE_MIGHTLING_ASK.md §2.3, §13). Every implementation of the policy runs every case with the same stubs, at the air-gap level the case names in `airgapped` ("off" when absent): a named prompt's composed text is the string "PROMPT:<name>"; the scratch folders it creates are "SCRATCH/1", "SCRATCH/2", ... in order of creation, counted across the whole file; and a thread whose id starts with "ask-" or "chat-" is an existing Ask thread whose folder is "ASK/<id>" (no other thread has one). A folder whose path starts with "WORK/" is a Work folder (an existing directory outside the Ask root), and no other is. `pending` lists the ids (as JSON text) of server requests waiting for an answer before the case. `out` is the exact message forwarded to the app-server, compared as JSON values; `pendingAfter` the ids still waiting after it.

cases.name: an allowed request passes unchanged, its jsonrpc field removed
a request outside the allow-list is refused
account sign-in is refused
remote control is refused
thread/start loses every dropped field
thread/resume and thread/fork lose the dropped fields too
the default prompt by name sets nothing: the launcher's catalog already carries it
a named prompt is turned into baseInstructions by the policy, never by the UI
an Ask thread gets its prompt, a fresh scratch folder as cwd and a sandbox rooted there; what the UI said about folders and permissions is ignored
each Ask thread gets a folder of its own
a phone bridge's thread (`chat`) is an Ask thread too: its prompt, a fresh scratch folder as cwd, a sandbox rooted there, and no approvals (a phone cannot wait on one; the sandbox has the network)
a phone's thread resumed (known by its folder, chat-…) keeps its config: no image search and no approvals, whatever the bridge asked
a phone's thread at airgapped on gets both configs: no plugins, no image search
a prompt name outside namedPrompts is refused
a prompt that is not a string is refused
a prompt on a request that is not a thread opener is refused
fields that load tools, environments, plugins or another history are dropped from every opener
thread/resume cannot load a forged history or rollout file
a prompt cannot be chosen on resume: a session keeps the prompt it started with
a resumed Ask thread stays in its folder, whatever the UI asks
a fork of an Ask thread stays in the Ask thread's folder
any other thread is resumed where the UI says
an allowed notification passes
any other notification is refused
an answer to a pending server request passes and is no longer pending
an answer to a request the server never made is refused: the UI cannot invent approvals
a string id and a number id are different requests
something that is not an object is refused
an object that is neither a request, a notification nor an answer is refused
review/start passes: /review runs on the server, inline or in a thread of its own (DESKTOP_PARITY item 6)
command/exec passes: a terminal tab is a PTY under the thread's permission profile (DESKTOP_PARITY item 8)
command/exec/write passes: keystrokes for a terminal tab
command/exec/resize passes: a terminal tab's new size
command/exec/terminate passes: a terminal tab closed
thread/shellCommand passes at /airgapped off: the user's own ! command, run in their shell as Codex runs it
thread/shellCommand is refused at /airgapped on (the level of the thread it names): it runs with no sandbox, so nothing would keep it off the network
thread/shellCommand is refused at on in an Ask thread too
thread/goal/set passes: the goal row sets, pauses and resumes a thread's goal (DESKTOP_PARITY item 5)
thread/goal/get passes: the goal row reads a thread's goal
thread/goal/clear passes: the goal row clears it
skills/config/write passes: a skill turned off or on (DESKTOP_PARITY item 11)
plugin/list passes: the local and repository marketplaces' plugins
plugin/install passes: a plugin from a local marketplace
plugin/uninstall passes
config/mcpServer/reload passes: MCP servers read again after a change
hooks/list passes: the lifecycle hooks, read only
thread/memoryMode/set passes: /memories in a thread (DESKTOP_PARITY item 13)
memory/status passes: Settings > Memories shows what is kept
memory/reset passes: Settings > Memories deletes them, on the user's click
fs/readDirectory passes: the file tree lists a folder (DESKTOP_PARITY Phase 3 item 1)
fs/readFile passes: a file tab or the artifacts viewer reads a file
fs/watch passes: the file tree follows a folder's changes
fs/unwatch passes: the file tree stops following a folder
externalAgentConfig/detect passes: Settings > Import finds another agent's configuration (Phase 3 item 8)
externalAgentConfig/import passes: the items the user ticked are imported
externalAgentConfig/import keeps its plugin items while airgapped is off: plugins are allowed
externalAgentConfig/import at airgapped on loses its plugin items, whose sources are cloned or fetched from the network; config and skills still import
externalAgentConfig/import of plugins alone at airgapped on is refused: nothing would be left to import
externalAgentConfig/import with an item that names no itemType is refused rather than guessed at
externalAgentConfig/import without a migrationItems list is refused
externalAgentConfig/import/readHistories passes: the past imports are listed
fs/writeFile is refused: the window reads files through the server and never writes them
fs/remove is refused: the window never deletes through the server
window tools named on thread/start become the policy's own dynamicTools; the UI's own dynamicTools are dropped

dynamicTools.name: mightling_terminal_output
dynamicTools.description: Read the recent output of the terminal tabs the user has open for this thread in the Mightling app (a dev server, a build, a test run): each tab's command line and its last lines of output, newest last. Use it to see what the user sees in their terminal instead of asking them to paste it. Secrets that look like tokens are masked.

lines.description: How many of the last lines of each tab to return (default 120).

dynamicTools.name: mightling_preview_console
dynamicTools.description: Read the browser console of the preview tabs the user has open in the Mightling app (a local dev server's page): each tab's address and its recent console messages and page errors, newest last. Use it to check a web page you changed. Secrets that look like tokens are masked.

lines.description: How many of the last messages of each tab to return (default 120).

cases.name: an empty list of window tools adds none
a window tool the policy does not define is refused
window tools named on thread/resume are refused: tools are set when a thread starts
externalAgentConfig/import of plugins alone passes while airgapped is off
plugin/install at airgapped on is refused: installing runs git outside the sandbox
marketplace/add passes while airgapped is off: a marketplace in a git repository
marketplace/add at airgapped on is refused
marketplace/upgrade passes while airgapped is off
marketplace/upgrade at airgapped on is refused: it asks the repository for news
marketplace/remove passes at airgapped on: it only deletes a folder
plugin/uninstall passes at airgapped on
plugin/read passes at airgapped on: it reads a marketplace already on disk
plugin/share/save is refused: sharing goes through the vendor's accounts
thread/start at airgapped on starts without plugins, whatever config the UI sent
thread/resume of an Ask thread at airgapped on stays in its folder and has no plugins
thread/fork at airgapped on has no plugins
thread/start while airgapped is off keeps the plugins: no config is added
thread/delete deletes a thread for good: allowed, unchanged (the server refuses an unknown or unsaved thread)
thread/delete is local, so it is allowed at airgapped on too
thread/delete naming a prompt is refused: a prompt is chosen only when a thread is started
thread/delete naming window tools is refused
an Ask thread's fork into a Work folder (a project's primary folder, DESKTOP §16 B33) goes there as a Work thread, with the Ask folder's sandbox
an Ask thread's fork into any other folder (another question's) does not go there: it stays in its own folder
an Ask thread's fork into a Work folder gets no broader sandbox or permissions than its own, and no other folders, whatever the UI asks
a resumed Ask thread stays in its folder even when the UI names a Work folder: only a fork moves
a phone's thread continued in a Work folder leaves its prompt's config (no approvals asked) behind
an Ask thread's fork into a Work folder at airgapped on has no plugins
a bridge thread/start with prompt chat-work and a cwd in repoCheckouts passes with approval policy on-request and workspace-write sandbox
a bridge thread/start with prompt chat-work and a cwd not in repoCheckouts is refused
a chat-work thread/start with no cwd is refused
a bridge thread/start with prompt default is refused
a bridge thread/start with no prompt is refused
a bridge thread/start with prompt chat (Ask) still passes as today, still with approval_policy never
a non-bridge chat-work thread/start in a checkout passes
a chat-work thread/start asking for danger-full-access ends up workspace-write
thread/resume of a thread in repoThreads gets on-request and workspace-write and pins cwd
thread/resume of another thread not in repoThreads is unchanged
thread/fork of a thread in repoThreads gets on-request and workspace-write and pins cwd
a bridge turn/start with a sandboxPolicy override has pinnedTurnFields removed
a page turn/start on a repo thread with an approvalPolicy override has pinnedTurnFields removed
a page turn/start on an ordinary thread keeps its overrides
thread/resume of a repo thread removes scratch fields and pins cwd to the recorded checkout
a bridge thread/resume of a thread that is neither Ask nor chat-work is refused
a bridge thread/fork of a thread that is neither Ask nor chat-work is refused
a bridge thread/resume of a recorded repo thread passes and pins cwd to the checkout
a chat-work thread/start in a read-only checkout gets read-only sandbox and on-request approvals
thread/resume of a repo thread in a read-only checkout gets read-only sandbox
a bridge's turn/start cannot choose an automated approvals reviewer
a page's chat-work thread/start cannot choose an automated approvals reviewer
a page turn/start on a repo thread cannot pick a permissions profile or add workspace roots
a bridge turn/start cannot pick a permissions profile
a page's chat-work thread/start drops a permissions profile and extra workspace roots
a granted repo thread turn/start gets an explicit dangerFullAccess sandboxPolicy
an ungranted repo thread turn/start gets an explicit workspaceWrite sandboxPolicy
a repo thread in a read-only checkout gets an explicit readOnly sandboxPolicy on turn/start
a granted repo thread asking for a permissions profile still gets only dangerFullAccess
an ungranted repo thread turn/start carries the user's workspace sandbox: its network and its writable roots
a repo thread in a read-only checkout keeps the user's network in its readOnly sandbox, and a grant never widens it
a messenger bridge's turn on a granted repo thread gets the workspace sandbox, never dangerFullAccess
params given as a list are refused: the app-server reads a list field by field, so it would carry a sandbox, approvals and instructions past the policy
a turn's params given as a list are refused, so a repository turn's sandbox cannot be set past the policy
params that are neither an object nor null are refused, a request's or a notification's
a phone bridge runs no command: command/exec with Full Access is refused
a phone bridge runs no ! command
a phone bridge writes no configuration: an MCP server's command is a host command
a phone bridge writes no configuration in a batch either
a phone bridge reads no file
a phone bridge installs no plugin
a phone bridge lists a thread's turns
the owner's window writes configuration
